summary: Fumihiko Sueki specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Yoshiro Tamura, Kyosho Hayashima, and Hajime Nakamura, later serving as professor at Tokyo, the International Research Center for Japanese Studies, and SOKENDAI.

Fumihiro Okada works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 2015) and was appointed as a specially appointed associate professor at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Fumimaro Watanabe worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University and the University of Toronto under Hammalawa Saddhatissa and A. K. Warder, later holding posts at Kindai University (1972–1981) and Aichi Gakuin University (1987).

Fumimasa Fukui specialized in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned degrees from Waseda University and the EPHE, studying under Paul Demiéville, Max Kaltenmark, and Rolf Alfred Stein. He served as a professor at Waseda University from ~1978 to 2005.
Fumio Enomoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a research assistant at Kyoto University (~1981–1987) and as a professor at Osaka University (~2000–2017).

Fumio Masutani worked in Buddhist and religious studies, earning degrees from the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1954–1968) and Taisho University (~1968–1973), and served as president of Tsuru University (1969–1971).

Fumio Ouchi specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He completed his doctoral studies at Otani University, where he served as associate professor (~1993–1998) and professor (~1998–2013).
Fumio Shoji is a scholar of Buddhist studies who was educated at Rissho University. He served there as an assistant professor from ~2013 to 2016 and became an associate professor in ~2016.
Fumio Tamamuro specializes in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Meiji University from ~1954 to 1963 and subsequently held a post there from ~1976 to 2006.

Futoshi Omae is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as a lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1991) and held a post at Shimane Prefectural Junior College of Nursing (attested 1997).
Futoshi Takehashi works in Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at Otani University (attested 1992) and served as an assistant at the Shinshu Otani-ha Research Institute from 1995 to 1997.
Fuyuan Luo is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who is a PhD student at the University of Cambridge under the supervision of Adam Yuet Chau (attested 2026).

Fyodor Buslaev worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the Faculty of History and Philology of Moscow University from ~1833 to 1838 and held a post at Moscow State University in 1846.

Fyodor Shcherbatskoy was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Ivan Minayev and Sergey Oldenburg, as well as under Georg Bühler and Hermann Jacobi, later serving as professor at Saint Petersburg (~1909–1941).

Félix Nève specialized in Indology and linguistics. He earned a doctorate at KU Leuven and studied under Christian Lassen, Friedrich Wilhelm Thiersch, and Eugène Burnouf, later serving as professor at KU Leuven from 1841 to 1877.

G. C. Nayak is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He held appointments as a fellow at the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (~1994–1997) and senior fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (1996).

G. Clinton Godart specializes in Japanology, history, and philosophy. He completed graduate studies at the University of Chicago under James Ketelaar, held posts at Needham Research Institute and the University of Southern California, and worked at Hokkaido University (attested 2017).
G. K. Jenkins was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Bloxham School (~1931–1936) and held a post at the British Museum from 1947 to 1978.

G. P. Malalasekera specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning degrees from the University of London and SOAS under Caroline Rhys Davids and William Stede. He held senior posts at Ceylon University College and the University of Ceylon.

G. Thomas Tanselle studied at Yale University. He taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1960–1978) and Columbia University (~1978–2004), and served as vice president of the John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation from 1978 to 2006.
